title: Peter Capaldi turned down Celebrity Traitors to avoid fame
snippet: Former Doctor Who actor declined to be on BBC's reality TV show because he did not want that 'level of exposure'

Log in or Subscribe Copy link X Icon twitter Facebook Icon facebook WhatsApp Icon whatsapp email Add us as preferred source Copy link X Icon twitter Facebook Icon facebook WhatsApp Icon whatsapp email Peter Capaldi said he was asked to be part of the Celebrity Traitors cast but he declined the offer Credit: Carlo Paloni/Getty Images Telegraph Reporters Published 12 April 2026 4:11pm BST Peter Capaldi said he turned down The Celebrity Traitors because he did not want that “level of exposure”.In a discussion about the pressures of fame and his career, The Thick Of It actor told the BBC’s Sunday With Laura Kuenssberg programme that he had been asked to take part in the all-star version of the BBC’s reality TV show, but said no.Capaldi, 67, said: “I think there’s a level of fame that… I think it propels you into the public eye at a level of exposure that I don’t really want.“I like doing, you know, it’s like doing my music things – it’s very difficult for people in that business to understand that you want to keep it small.“People keep saying to me, ‘why don’t you do a bigger tour?’, or ‘why don’t you do a bigger release?’, or ‘why don’t you promote this more?’ And I don’t… I’m not doing it to be famous.” Peter Capaldi played the Twelfth Doctor between 2014 and 2017 Credit: Ray Burmiston/BBC In his previous leading role as Doctor Who, Capaldi said he had “a little regret” when asked if he had left the BBC sci-fi show too early. He played the Twelfth Doctor in the show for three series between 2014-2017.He said he enjoyed being Doctor Who, but admitted that the pressure was “quite intense” because he didn’t want to “disappoint anyone”.“Yeah, because I’m quite miserable and melancholic, really,” he joked, adding: “And that was one of the big changes in my life, I guess, which happened quite late, was I’m quite miserable, really, but I thought you can’t be miserable if you’re Doctor Who.“You can’t because you would disappoint people, so I have to become cheerful all the time.”The first series of The Celebrity Traitors aired on the BBC last autumn, with its finale attracting a peak 15.4 million viewers, according to the broadcaster.Its cast of celebrities included Celia Imrie and Nick Mohammed, both actors, Paloma Faith, the singer, Stephen Fry, the author and actor, Jonathan Ross, the broadcaster and Alan Carr, the comedian who went on to win as a Traitor.The spin-off series, hosted by Claudia Winkleman, brought in an average audience of 14.9 million people during its run – the biggest TV audience of 2025.
